Runs configured fix tools on specified files or the entire project.
Tools are executed based on priority and file patterns, with automatic parallelization
for non-overlapping tasks.

Use --explain to see the execution plan without running:
  --explain          Show brief plan (summary mode, default)
  --explain=summary  Show brief plan
  --explain=detailed Show detailed plan with file lists
  --explain=json     Output plan in JSON format

Usage:
  datamitsu fix [files...] [flags]

Flags:
      --allow-partial                Write a report that lists findings for a narrowed run (named files, a subdirectory, --tools, --file-scoped) instead of refusing it; the report keeps every reason it is incomplete (also via DATAMITSU_ALLOW_PARTIAL)
      --annotations string           Print the run's findings as workflow annotations once it ends: auto (github in a GitHub Actions job, unless stdout carries a document or --log-format jsonl is on), github or off (also via DATAMITSU_ANNOTATIONS) (default "auto")
      --events string                Which findings --log-format jsonl carries as diagnostic events: diagnostics=reported (at or above failOn, the default) or diagnostics=all (also via DATAMITSU_EVENTS)
      --explain string[="summary"]   Show execution plan without running (summary|detailed|json)
      --fail-fast                    Stop at the first failing tool; --fail-fast=false runs everything to the end (also via DATAMITSU_FAIL_FAST) (default true)
      --fail-on string               Fail on findings at this level or above in every operation (error|warning|info|hint); raises an operation's failOn, never lowers it (also via DATAMITSU_FAIL_ON)
      --fail-on-skip                 Exit non-zero if any tool is skipped because its binary is unavailable for this platform
      --file-scoped                  Only process git staged files
  -h, --help                         help for fix
      --output string                How the run shows its results: human (frames, colour, progress) or agent (one line per finding the terminal would show, one summary line per operation; also via DATAMITSU_OUTPUT) (default "human")
      --report stringArray           Write a report once the run ends, failed or not: <format>=<path>, or <format>=- for stdout (repeatable; formats: json, junit, markdown, sarif; turns fail-fast off; also via DATAMITSU_REPORT)
      --require-coverage string      Exit non-zero unless the run answered completely (unit|repo)
      --tools string                 Comma-separated list of tools to run (for debugging)
      --widen-to string              Limit how far work may widen beyond the selection (target|unit|repo)

Global Flags:
      --before-config strings   Configuration file(s) to load before auto-discovery (for wrappers/libraries)
      --binary-command string   Override the binary command (for npm package wrappers, etc). Can also be set via DATAMITSU_BINARY_COMMAND env var
      --config strings          Additional configuration file(s) to load and merge (can be specified multiple times)
      --log-format string       Status output format: console or jsonl (also via DATAMITSU_LOG_FORMAT)
      --no-auto-config          Disable auto-discovery of datamitsu.config.{js,mjs,ts} at git root
      --no-oci                  Disable OCI bundle store seeding (also via DATAMITSU_NO_OCI)
      --no-parse                Show tools' raw output instead of parsed findings; parsing still runs (also via DATAMITSU_NO_PARSE)
  -v, --verbose                 Enable debug-level logging (default level is warn)
